sections.title: Unit 18: Rhetoric, Framing & Mass Persuasion
body: From parliamentary addresses and election campaign manifestos to advertising slogans and landmark legal arguments, the art of persuasion relies heavily on framing. In Hungarian, the syntactical engine of framing is the cataphoric clause: a case-marked demonstrative pronoun in the main clause that points forward to an explanatory or subjunctive hogy-clause.

In this unit, you will master Hungarian cataphoric anchors (arra, abban, ahhoz, azzal + hogy), learn how abstract nouns combine with demonstratives to define institutional postures (azon az állásponton van, hogy; arra a következtetésre jutott, hogy), analyze how rhetorical framing shifts agency and emotion, and deconstruct formal public speeches inspired by classic Hungarian political oratory.
